speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs whether the current political situation in Malaysia has any implications for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs in light of Malaysia’s recent change of government (a) whether he can provide an update on our bilateral ties with Malaysia; and (b) how the Government will move forward on the many bilateral partnerships with Malaysia such as the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System Link and COVID-19 border control measures.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Our long-term relationship will always be bound by the ties of kinship, culture, history and economic interdependence.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: A stable and prosperous Malaysia is good for Singapore and indeed, good for our region.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Naturally, the Singapore Government watches developments in Malaysia very closely.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As Members of the House would be aware, there has been a change in leadership in Malaysia.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Many Singapore Ministers have also established or renewed contact with their Malaysian counterparts.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Singapore’s consistent position is to work with the government of the day.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Our leaders are familiar with Prime Minister Ismail Sabri and his Cabinet members.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We have worked with them on many bilateral and regional issues.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Prime Minister Ismail Sabri and I have known each other from the days when we were both the Ministers for Youth and Sports.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We also met during my more recent visit to Malaysia in March earlier this year, when we discussed COVID-19 safeguards and cross-border travel arrangements.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: My counterpart – Minister of Foreign Affairs Saifuddin Abdullah – is also a familiar face.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We worked closely together when he held the Foreign Affairs portfolio between 2018 and 2020.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Besides the political leadership, our respective civil service maintains good relations and communications with each other and officials on both sides are in regular contact.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Construction has in fact commenced on both sides and there has been good progress.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We look forward to it significantly improving connectivity between Singapore and Johor Bahru, and easing congestion on the Causeway.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We are continuing discussions with the Malaysian government on the safe and gradual resumption of cross-border movement of people as we enter the endemic phase.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This will require mutually agreed public health protocols to preserve the public health and safety of residents on both sides, whilst taking into account the medical resources available.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: These discussions have been fruitful and we hope that this can map our path forward for a safe and gradual reopening of our borders when the situation permits it.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Singapore and Malaysia will always be closely intertwined and interdependent.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We are committed to engaging and cooperating with the new Malaysian government to seek win-win outcomes.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is especially important in order for both our countries to recover and emerge stronger together from the COVID-19 pandemic situation.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I am confident that our bilateral cooperation will continue to expand for the mutual benefit of citizens on both sides.
